deck.request: Why are ambulance response times rising, and where should the first new crews go? Use only the board papers we have sent you.
deck.brief: Why are ambulance response times rising, and where should the first new crews go?
deck.answer: Calls per crew and hospital handover delay drive the rise in response times; the first new crews go to Uplands and Valley, nearest the 18-minute standard, with handover delay cut alongside so the new crews are not held at hospital.

pages.title: Calls per crew and handover delay drive the rise; Uplands and Valley get crews first
pages.why: The opening states why response times rose, where the first crews go and the condition on them

settles.what: response time, calls, crews and handover delay from 2023 Q1 to 2024 Q4, and the two slowest districts

pages.adds: Each point says what its finding means for where the crews go and what must change beside them
pages.highlight: handover delay has to be cut alongside
points: Mean response time rose {{B-rise/percent | 0%}} in two years to {{o-response/response@2024 Q4 | 0.0}} minutes. On the two-year trend it breaches the {{o-standard/standard | 0}}-minute national standard in 2028.

Two causes drive the rise. Calls rose {{B-calls/percent | 0%}} while crews on shift fell, so each crew answers a quarter more calls; and hospital handover more than doubled to {{o-handover/handover@2024 Q4 | 0}} minutes, holding crews off the road.

The first new crews go to Uplands and Valley, the districts nearest the standard. Because a crew held at hospital cannot take the next call, handover delay has to be cut alongside, or the new crews will wait at the door too.
The board papers hold no district figures for demand or handover, so the order of districts rests on response time alone.

pages.title: Send the first crews to Uplands and Valley, and cut handover delay alongside
items: Send the first new crews to Uplands, then Valley: they have the least headroom before a breach of the national standard.
Cut handover delay at the emergency departments alongside, since a crew held at the door adds no cover however many are hired.
Track calls per crew on shift each quarter, the measure that says whether the new crews keep pace with demand.
Ask the service for district figures on demand and handover before the second wave of crews is placed.
